newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MATAV TO INVEST $400 TO 500 MLN IN '97; IPO PENDING.
newsitem.headline: MATAV TO INVEST $400 TO 500 MLN IN '97; IPO PENDING.

text.p: Hungarian telecommunications company Matav Rt sees better-than-planned 1996 results but has not yet decided on an equity offering, an official said on Monday.
"We had a very good year," Matav's chief financial officer Ray Stewart told Reuters in an interview in which he outlined the company's capital investment plans.
Stewart also said there had been no decision yet on choosing a financial adviser for an equity offering that Matav may make this year.
He said he had seen a Financial Times article which said Matav was set to name Merrill Lynch to lead the international equity offering, but would not confirm it.
"We are still talking to different banks about a possible role, in a possible Matav IPO, but no decision has been made yet," he said.

Matav in October said it expected profits of more that 12 billion forints in 1996 on net sales of 190 billion forints compared with a net profit of 293 million forints on sales of 135.5 billion in 1995. The company made vast capital outlays in 1995 to upgrade its aging system and to expand.
Based on net sales ranking, Matav was the third biggest Hungarian company in 1995, behind oil and gas company MOL Rt and electricity company MVM.
He said they plan a capital investment programme of some $400 to $500 million this year, mainly towards network improvement.
"We will build new lines, new digital exchanges and will also put in additional data line and data processing for businesses," Stewart said.
Stewart added that the first step towards an equity offering -- choosing the financial adviser -- will probably be taken at the end of January.
"For sure I'm hoping we will have it finished by the end of this month," he said.

Geza Laszlo chief economist of Matav's financial arm, Investel, said last November that CS First Boston, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Merrill Lynch and Morgan Stanley are shortlisted to be the financial adviser.
The Financial Times in London reported earlier that Matav is set to name Merrill Lynch to lead the equity offering.
Stewart said it was premature to discuss the size of a public offering since there was as yet no decision on whether there would be an IPO.

"Once that decision (of choosing the financial adviser) has been made, it has to be decided whether it is MagyarCom that would sell shares, is it the government or is it the company issuing new equity?" he said. "All of these impact the size (of a prospective offering)".
Deutsche Telekom and Ameritech together bought 30 percent of Matav in 1993 for $850 million and purchased another 37 percent of the company in late 1995 for $852 million.

The Hungarian government holds a 25 percent stake with the remainder held by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the International Finance Corporation, local governments and individual investors.
An analyst said the market is looking forward to the Matav offering which could be all the more attractive if the state also decides to sell some of its stake.
"It could be a share package of some $1 billion, which would be the biggest Hungarian offering so far," Voros said.
He added that Matav has also had good results when compared to other telecommunications companies in central Europe.

"The only other company in the region it could be compared with is the Czech Republic's SPT Telecom ," Voros said."Although SPT also invests very large amounts in its network, I think Matav is ahead of them."
